rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A microscope uses a short-focus objective on a near object, and its magnification is about (L/f_o)(D/f_e). A telescope uses a long-focus objective on a distant object, and for a relaxed eye its power is f_o/f_e with tube length f_o + f_e.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Governing equation for "Optical instruments — microscope and telescope" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
Microscope m ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e)
Telescope m = f_o / f_e for the relaxed eye

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: D = 25 cm unless the question says otherwise.  ·  The final image at infinity means the eye is relaxed.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A compound microscope has two convex lenses. The objective has a short focal length and makes a real, enlarged image of a nearby object. The eyepiece is used as a magnifier on that image.  ·  When the final image is at the near point D, about 25 cm, the magnification is approximately (L/f_o)(D/f_e), where L is the tube length between the two lenses. A shorter objective focal length gives a larger magnification.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Compound microscope  ·  Astronomical telescope  ·  Magnifying power  ·  Relaxed eye

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: A microscope magnifies a near, tiny object.  ·  A telescope magnifies a distant, large object.  ·  Both use an objective and an eyepiece.  ·  The final image is at infinity for the relaxed eye.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: answer pattern for "Optical instruments — microscope and telescope": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What is the telescope tube length in that setting?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A microscope has f_o = 1.0 cm, f_e = 5.0 cm and L = 20 cm. Take D = 25 cm. Estimate the magnification with m = (L/f_o)(D/f_e).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: A microscope objective has → B  ·  Relaxed-eye telescope power is → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: An astronomical telescope looks at a distant object, so the rays arrive nearly parallel. The objective makes a real image in its focal plane. A long objective focal length gathers a large image.  ·  For the relaxed eye the final image is at infinity, and the magnifying power is f_o / f_e. A long objective and a short eyepiece give a large power. The tube length is then about f_o + f_e.  ·  The microscope wants a short, strong objective. The telescope wants a long objective. Swapping those choices is the usual mix-up.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The microscope objective is short, not long.  ·  Telescope power is f_o/f_e, not f_e/f_o.  ·  The relaxed-eye tube length is f_o + f_e, not the microscope's L.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: D is 25 cm, the near point, not the focal length.  ·  Name the instrument before the formula.  ·  f_o and f_e must be in the same unit.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write Microscope m ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e) and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.
